summary: Quick acne follow-up where one medicine is stopped and one is added. Trap: doxycycline is stopped for acidity and must not appear as a prescription row (medication history is fine).

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Come, sit. So how are the pimples now, any better?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Little better doctor, but new ones are still coming on the cheeks. And that doxycycline tablet is giving me acidity, burning in the chest.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Then we will stop the doxycycline completely. Don't take it from today.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes. Instead I am starting Sotret, isotretinoin, ten milligram capsule. One capsule once daily after dinner, for one month.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, with food, it absorbs better. Your lips will become dry, so keep a lip balm. Before next visit, get a lipid profile done.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My lips are already dry. And I go out in the sun daily for college.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Use any plain lip balm many times a day, and a cap in the sun. No squeezing the pimples. Theek hai?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay doctor. And the lipid profile test before next visit, right?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And come back to see me after four weeks with the report.
